# clavis login

<p class="cli-lead">Sign in with a browser (device code)</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis login [flags]
```

</div>

Sign in with your browser. Clavis shows a short code, opens the approval
page, and saves the token in the OS keychain (or in the file named by
`CLAVIS_CREDENTIAL_FILE`). The server is remembered, so later commands
don't need `--server`.

On a machine without a browser (SSH session, container), pass
`--no-browser` and open the printed link on any other device.

If the server uses a self-signed certificate (`CLAVIS_TLS=self-signed`,
common on a LAN), `login` shows the certificate's fingerprint and asks
whether to trust it. The answer is remembered for this server, so you
are asked once per computer. See [`clavis trust`](./trust).

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">Sign in to your server</p>

```sh
clavis login --server https://clavis.example.com
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Sign in from an SSH session</p>

```sh
clavis login --server https://clavis.example.com --no-browser
```

## Flags

<dl class="cli-flags">
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-no-browser"><dt><code>--no-browser</code></dt><dd>do not open the browser automatically</dd></div>
</dl>

## Details

In CI and other automation, don't log in: set `CLAVIS_TOKEN` to a machine
token instead. See [environment variables](./environment-variables).
